newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell 61 pct of Kherson oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell 61 pct of Kherson oil refinery.

text.p: Ukraine will sell a 61 percent stake in its Kherson oil refinery in the south to foreign and local strategic investors, a State Property Fund (FDM) official said on Monday.
Yosyf Voytsekhovsky, deputy director of the fund's sales department, said a date for the tender, for stakes of 30 and 31 percent, was not set, but he said it could take place in July.
A government plan for the refinery, one of six in Ukraine and the former Soviet republic's third largest, would keep 10 percent of shares in government hands.
Workers and managers would keep 23.82 percent and 5.18 percent would be sold through privatisation certificates.
Kherson refined 1.46 million tonnes (29,200 barrels per day) of oil last year, compared to 2.29 million tonnes (45,800 bpd) in 1995.
It has an annual capacity of 8.2 million tonnes (164,000 bpd).
Officials said the refinery, built in 1949, planned to modernise soon. Its most recent renovation was in 1974.
Ukraine's six refineries have a total annual refining capacity of up to 60 million tonnes (1.2 million bpd).
Privatisation of the other five refineries has already started.
